To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the population-wide spread and the total number of drug-resistant infections can be minimized if the initial prevalence of drug-sensitive strains under low pressure of drug is followed by a timely and intensive drug treatment, (ii) the effectiveness of this strategy depends on the initial prevalence of sensitive strains, the efficacy of the drugs and the duration of the treatment, (iii) the effectiveness of the treatment strategy is robust to the presence of pre-existing immunity.

(1) a sizable portion of the population must be depleted before drugs are administered on a large scale to avoid the spread of drug-resistant strains; and (2) the initial prevalence of drug-sensitive strain, followed by the timely implementation of intensive treatments, can minimize the number of infections and prevent the outbreaks of drug-resistant infection.

, for the treatment of infectious diseases caused by pathogens with high rates of mutation, the management of drug-resistant infections in the population may require an early depletion of susceptible hosts to minimize the number of infections and to prevent the spread of drug resistance.
